title: WPMS/1104/2024 of ADITYA VASHISHT Vs DINESH KUMAR GUPTA

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings or
directions and
Registrar's order with
Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No.1104 of 2024
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the
petitioners.
2. Mr. Arvind Vashishtha, Senior Advocate
assisted by Ms. Disha Vashishtha, Advocate for
the respondent no.1 would submit that he is
withdrawing himself from the case.
3. Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate would
submit that he has received instructions to appear
on behalf of respondent no.1. He files his
Vakalatnama, which is taken on record.
4. This writ petition has been filed for
quashing of judgment and order dated 15.04.2024
passed by Board of Revenue, Uttarakhand,
Dehradun in Revision No.85/2022-2023 "Aditya
Vashishta and Ors. vs. Dinesh Gupta and Ors."
whereby the revision filed by the petitioners has
been dismissed. Further, quashing of order dated
23.08.2023 (wrongly written as 09.08.2023 in the
prayer clause) passed by Additional
Commissioner, Garhwal Mandal, Camp
Dehradun in Revision No.44/2022-23 has been
sought, whereby the revision filed by respondent
no.1 was allowed.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners and
respondent no.1 would jointly submit that they
are only contesting parties in this case.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners would
submit that Suit No.12/2006-2007 was filed by
predecessors-in-interest of respondent nos.2, 3, 4,
6 and 7 and respondent nos.5 and 8 against the
defendants including defendant no.6/1,

defendants nos.6/2 and defendant no.6/3 i.e. the
petitioners seeking partition of agricultural land;
that, during the pendency of suit respondent
no.9/defendant no.1 is purported to have
executed sale deeds in favour of several persons,
who were impleaded as defendant nos.8 to 13 in
the suit; that, the plaintiff nos.1/1, 1/2 and 1/3 i.e.
respondent nos.2, 3 and 4 and plaintiff no.4 i.e.
respondent no.5 filed applications before the
Assistant Collector (Ist Class) for withdrawal of
the suit; that, the respondent no.1/ defendant
no.11 then filed an application under Order I
Rule 10 of CPC seeking his transposition as
plaintiffs to the suit.
7. Learned counsel would further submit that
the learned Assistant Collector I Class, vide order
dated 04.08.2023, dismissed the suit as
withdrawn (Annexure-9).
8. He would further submit that the petitioner
no.1/defendant no.6/1 filed a caveat (Annexure-10) before Additional Commissioner, Garhwal
Mandal, Dehradun as against respondent
no.1/defendant no.11 in the suit; that, respondent
no.1/defendant no.11 filed Revision No.44 of
2022-23 against the order dated 04.08.2023; that,
the Additional Commissioner while hearing the
revision at the admission stage, allowed the
revision by order dated 23.08.2023 and the order
dated 04.08.2023 was set aside; that, being
aggrieved petitioners preferred Revision
No.85/2023 before the Board of Revenue; that,
the Board of Revenue, vide impugned order
dated 15.04.2024, dismissed the revision of the
petitioners.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners would
submit that before filing of the revision by the

respondent no.1/defendant no.11 before the
Additional Commissioner, Garhwal Division, a
caveat had already been filed by petitioner
no.1/defendant no.6/1 but the Additional
Commissioner without issuing notice to the
parties and without granting opportunity of
hearing to the caveator/petitioner, allowed the
revision, which is illegal and unjustified; that,
this fact was also not considered by the Board of
Revenue and the revision filed by the petitioners
was dismissed in a very cursory and mechanical
manner.
10. At this stage, learned counsel for
respondent no.1/defendant no.11 would submit
that the writ petition may be allowed and the
order dated 04.08.2023 may be upheld with
liberty to the respondent no.1/defendant no.11 to
file a suit for partition in respect of his undivided
share in the property in question.
11. In view of the consent given by counsel for
respondent no.1/defendant no.11, writ petition is
allowed. Impugned orders dated 23.08.2023 and
15.04.2024 are hereby set aside. Order dated
04.08.2023 is upheld.
12. Liberty is given to respondent
no.1/defendant no.11 to file a suit for partition in
respect of his undivided share in the property in
question or to pursue any other legal remedy
available to him as per law.
